description: We are exploring ways to help humanity with NISAR data.
summary:
Sinking Ground maps subsidence measured by NASA and ISRO’s NISAR satellite across 745 cities, down to buildings at risk. Search any address, then act: 
Get a one page report as proof, send a ready written letter to the responsible office in nine languages, and join or start a neighbourhood group.

https://github.com/Ottitsch/nasa-space-apps

What it does

Sinking Ground is a global map of ground that is sinking, measured by NISAR. For each place it answers three questions: where is the ground going down and how fast, which built up areas and buildings sit on ground that sinks unevenly enough to crack them and when do they pass the damage limits, and how sure are we. Pick a place on the globe or type an address, drag the time bar through every radar pass (one every 12 days) and on along a projection to 2050, and zoom to street level to see individual buildings coloured by risk class. Click anywhere to read the rate, how far that spot has sunk and when it passes each limit.

How it works

A Python pipeline searches NASA's CMR catalogue for NISAR L2 GUNW interferograms over each place and reads only the HDF5 chunks it needs remotely (about 25 MB instead of 2 GB per product). It keeps built up and bare ground with stable coherence (ESA WorldCover), removes orbit and atmosphere errors, inverts a small baseline network into a time series, combines ascending and descending tracks, and detects sinking only where the rate clears three times the map noise and a seasonal allowance that depends on the record length. Uneven sinking is measured as angular distortion and compared with classic foundation engineering limits (1/500, 1/300, 1/150). The result is exported as small 80 m grids that a web app loads.

Addresses no place covers are measured on request: a Cloudflare Pages Function starts a GitHub Actions job that runs the same pipeline over a 56 km box and publishes it for everyone in around 5 minutes. Only a coarse grid point leaves the device, never the address.

Results

745 places processed. At least 1 km² of built up land is detected sinking in 79, led by Mexico City and the Tehran Plain at 26 cm per year. Mexico City matches the map NASA and JPL published in 2026, and its two independent viewing directions agree to about 1.5 cm per year.

Benefits and impact

Seeing the problem is step zero. The take action page turns any spot into a one page PDF report, a ready written letter to the office responsible that cites the law obliging a reply, and a way for neighbours to form and list their own groups. Eighteen cities have a full local guide and the page exists in nine languages. Nothing the person types leaves their device.

Creativity and what we considered

Honesty about uncertainty is built in: every place shows the smallest rate its record can detect, short records are marked as early results, sinking assumed from before NISAR is labelled as an estimate and can be switched off, and places where a summer record could mistake shrinking clay for sinking are held back. We tested and rejected adding farmland because soil moisture read as false sinking. We also considered privacy, places where messaging apps are blocked, and the limits of an 80 m pixel: it is a screening map for neighbourhoods, not a verdict on a single building.

Tools

Python (NumPy, h5py), NISAR L2 GUNW via NASA Earthdata and CMR, JavaScript, MapLibre GL JS, PMTiles, Cloudflare Pages and Functions, GitHub Actions. Code was written with the help of Claude (Anthropic); translations were written by a language model and are marked as not yet checked by native speakers.
